Historical source: The Eryndor World Bible. --- ## Complete topic reference — preserved from the preceding edition This page records broad historical canon, ancient civilisations, established historical accounts, disputed traditions and accepted seeds for future discoveries. It is separate from the dated campaign chronicle and from the present-day investigation of the eastern mine. ## Moon-system scale retcon — 8.5× (creator decision, 21 November 2026) New current lunar population scale: Increase the present-day natural-satellite count by 8.5-fold over the earlier provisional 26–30 moons. This yields approximately 221–255 current moons; 238 is the convenient working midpoint (28 × 8.5), not a separately confirmed exact astronomical census. The old 26–30 count and its categories of four major, seven medium, ten small, five-to-nine tiny are superseded drafts; the size-class breakdown of the expanded system is open. Many may be small, tiny, distant or inconspicuous rather than hundreds of equally enormous moons; the sky, ring visibility, orbital stability, tides and physical hierarchy need careful later design consistent with ordinary everyday physics. Preserved cosmology: Ilyra and Vaelis remain established moons. The broad planetary ring system and ancient lunar collisions remain. Every moon has its own lunar magical influence/discipline as before, but the hundreds of individual domains, names, orbital positions and relations are not automatically invented or known. Eryndor still produces intrinsic Natural Magic independently of the satellites. The initial Great Cataclysm at the end of the First Age may have involved dozens of moons colliding across the sky—a creator-proposed scenario, not settled collision physics; an even larger ancient pre-cataclysm moon count is possible but not quantified. Later collisions are distinct. No fixed culprit moon is assigned to the Veiled Inland Sea. These are worldbuilding changes, not discoveries or elapsed time in Gloin's campaign. ## Great Cataclysm — proposed simultaneous multiple-moon collision scenario (21 November 2026) Established: The first great lunar catastrophe—the Great Cataclysm—marks the end of Eryndor's First Age and the beginning of the Second Age. Eryndor later experienced other lunar collisions; its current rings contain debris from ancient lunar destruction, and its magic responds to individual moons. Creator's newly suggested scenario, NOT yet fixed as historical detail: During the initial Great Cataclysm, dozens of moons could have collided or shattered essentially simultaneously across different parts of the sky, not merely a single two-moon impact. This might involve multiple direct collisions, secondary destruction and a dramatically more crowded ancient moon system. The current approximately 221–255 surviving moons (working midpoint 238) are not a cap on pre-cataclysm moons. Planetwide physical and magical consequences could have been complex and different by region; no exact number, trigger, timing precision, orbital mathematics, casualties, magical domains, responsible agent, or connection to later mysteries is established. Do not turn this plausible spectacular version into a confirmed astronomical reconstruction until the creator chooses it explicitly. ## First Age — one continuous Age, no eras; unknown length and reputed prosperity (creator decision, 21 November 2026) Creator canon: The First Age was one undivided Age, with no eras whatsoever. No formal, local, kingdom-specific, regional or historical era subdivisions are established within it; when constructing the official historical framework, do not invent a First Age era chronology. Its duration is entirely unknown, although later peoples and scholars guess it lasted thousands and thousands of years. Its characterization as a grand Age of Prosperity is later tradition and belief, not a historically verified description. Unbreakable source limitation: No records survive from before the first Great Cataclysm; therefore no surviving first-hand chronicles, inscriptional testimony, celestial logs, magical recordings or documented calendrical conversions prove First Age chronology, rulers, origins or level of prosperity. Do not invent a precise length, specific First Age civilization or definite name for its people as fact. The first Great Cataclysm ended the First Age and began the Second Age. Exactly which moons were involved and the catastrophe's causes remain open. Separate Second Age rule: The Second Age lasted exactly 1,437 years. The Avarran chronology divides it into three established eras: Awakening (321 years), Wonder (1,000 years), and Fire (116 years). These are Avarran era names and divisions, not compulsory terms or divisions for other continents. Three eras are Second Age only and must never be projected onto the First Age. This distinction supplements, rather than overrides, the general rule that worldwide Ages and locally dated eras are different concepts. The First Throne chronology, Gloin's ancestry and campaign remain unresolved/unchanged. ## First Age is undocumented — no surviving records before the Great Cataclysm (creator canon, 21 November 2026) ABSOLUTE CREATOR RULE: There are NO surviving records of any kind from before the First Great Cataclysm, which ended Eryndor's First Age and began the Second Age. No authenticated written histories, inscriptions, books, archives, celestial logs, eyewitness testimonies, preserved magical recordings or other verifiable contemporaneous records from the pre-Cataclysm First Age have survived into the known world. Never invent or let a current historian discover a surviving first-Age chronicle or first-hand recording as an ordinary source, and never treat a pre-Cataclysm date, monarch, civilization, religion, magic system or technological level as documentarily established. Knowledge and mythology: Later civilizations know the Great Cataclysm occurred and ended the First Age through post-Cataclysm evidence, reconstruction and traditions, not through surviving First Age testimony. Oral legends, religious creation tales or speculative scholarly reconstructions may claim to describe earlier times but are not verified records of that era; their credibility, accuracy and independent origins remain open. Even extraordinary physical remnants, if ever posited as a future story direction, are not by themselves surviving documentary records; no specific identifiable first-Age archaeological site is created by this rule. The earliest surviving documentary history is Second Age or later, unless the creator explicitly revises this principle. Canon safeguarding: The first lunar collision's exact moons, cause, chronological date, physical changes, all earlier civilizations and how life existed before the catastrophe remain unknown. The previously proposed simultaneous shattering of dozens of moons is still only a possibility, not an authenticated fact. The First Throne's recorded history and Silence Below retain their own open timeline; do not place them in the undocumented First Age without creator authorization. Gloin's ancestry remains entirely undetermined and cannot be inferred through this gap. No in-story time advances. ## First Age ending — the original lunar Great Cataclysm (creator decision, 21 November 2026) Established high-level historical event: The very first great collision among Eryndor's moons in the ancient lunar history is the Great Cataclysm. Its worldwide consequences mark the end of the First Age and the beginning of the Second Age. This refers to the initial catastrophic moon collision, not any of the later lunar collisions or close-approach incidents that also occurred in deep antiquity. The first impact destroyed or shattered lunar bodies, contributed to the vast planetary debris rings, and profoundly changed the magical environment of the planet. The lunar system's later collisions, fragments and magical consequences remain possible separate events, not automatically ends of their own Ages. Preserved open history: The absolute date and duration of the First Age, identities and exact orbits of the original colliding moons, number of casualties, continent conditions, civilizations present, and complete causal sequence are not established. Do not force the First Throne, all ruins, or Gloin's ancestry to be connected to this cataclysm. The Third, Fourth and Fifth Age transitions remain unwritten. This ancient event does not progress present-day campaign time. The present date remains Autumn Day 22, Year 3847 of the Era of Crowns, Fifth Age. ## Era of Awakening — THREE simultaneous lunar-magical consequences, definitive correction (21 November 2026) Latest binding creator correction: The 321-year Era of Awakening at the start of Eryndor's 1,437-year Second Age was defined by all three, equally essential, transformations following the First Great Cataclysm: 1. PERMANENT LOSS: Before the Great Cataclysm, Eryndor had vastly more moons than the modern surviving roughly 221–255; the exact original count is unknown. When original moons were destroyed and their particular magical sources ceased to exist, entire associated forms of lunar magic were truly and irreversibly lost to Eryndor. These are not merely forgotten spells, temporarily weakened techniques, or powers awaiting rediscovery. Only First Age peoples could ever have witnessed or used certain such lost powers. No First Age records survive, so modern people cannot establish a reliable exhaustive roster or reconstruct those disappeared disciplines from intact original accounts. 2. BIRTH OF NEW MAGIC: Some fragments of shattered moons settled into new separate orbiting bodies — new “moons” — and became new sources of lunar magic with powers or disciplines not present before. The Cataclysm thus irreversibly reshaped the roster of lunar magics in both directions; it was simultaneously a destruction and a creation. The exact new-moon tally, identities, paths of formation, and individual disciplines remain unspecified. Other debris contributed to Eryndor's existing planetary rings; not every fragment becomes a magically potent moon. 3. UNRELIABILITY AND UPHEAVAL: In addition to those permanent changes, lunar magic was profoundly unstable and unreliable in the post-Cataclysm upheaval: some surviving powers fluctuated, faltered, became dangerous or unpredictable, and the newly arising lunar sources were poorly understood. Inconsistency and risk were a central reason many peoples learned that even powerful working magic could not be the only reliable foundation of agriculture, healing, infrastructure, water, food, defense, or daily survival. This does not force every existing power to fail everywhere at once or mean that all magic remains equally unstable forever. Different peoples' responses include nonmagical resilience, engineering, new magical inquiry and adaptations of existing traditions. Critical continuity: All three consequences matter, rather than replacing unreliability with lost/new magic or reducing permanently destroyed disciplines to temporarily unstable magic. The planet's independent Natural Magic / World's Breath remains extant; culturally distinct magical arts of Khazari, Eldar, Aelwyn, Gnomes, Pixies, etc. remain where they can function without annihilated lunar sources. The first Age lasted an unknown time, had no internal eras, and has no surviving records; it is only believed by later peoples to have been an exceptionally long age of prosperity. The specific count of moons destroyed, when and how fragments became stable new moons, and detailed lunar-magic mechanics are open. The moon-shattering, loss/birth of distinct powers, and instability are established as historical realities, even though surviving post-Cataclysm scholars may never have complete proof of every pre-Cataclysm discipline. Modern planetscape has roughly 221–255 moons (midpoint \~238), not an exact confirmed count. The Second Age's second era is the 1,000-year Era of Wonder (Years 322–1,321); the Era of Fire lasted 116 years (Years 1,322–1,437). Do not retroactively connect the first throne mystery, Gloin's ancestry or any unapproved political narrative to the Cataclysm. ## Meaning of the Era of Awakening — lunar magical upheaval and the end of unquestioning reliance (creator direction, 21 November 2026) Creator-established central historical meaning: The Era of Awakening is named for the surviving peoples' realization, following the first Great Cataclysm, that magic was not an infallible foundation on which to rely for every necessity of life or government. The lunar collisions and destruction of magical source-moons caused an extraordinary upheaval in lunar magic, with lost or disrupted influences, unfamiliar changes, fluctuating effectiveness, unpredictable consequences and dangerous episodes. The exact magical physics of each disrupted source, spell or moon remain unknown; this does not assert that all disciplines failed simultaneously or that every place experienced the same severity. The awakening was philosophical and practical, not the initial discovery of magical powers: Post-Cataclysm peoples had to learn that if magic weakened, misbehaved or became unavailable for a particular task, ordinary material knowledge and workable contingencies still mattered. Reliably supplied food, water, shelter, medicine, roads, sanitation, mechanical systems, agriculture, trade, craftsmanship, engineering, recordkeeping and nonmagical fortifications could not be casually neglected. The cultural response varied across civilizations; magical research, religious reassessment, practical crafts, rebuilding and resilience could proceed together, often unevenly and through conflict. This is the conceptual reason for the 321-year first era of the 1,437-year Second Age (Second Age years 1–321). The era is not prescribed to have been universally peaceful or wholly technological. Important existing magic safeguard: Lunar moons are actual sources of lunar magic. Eryndor's Natural Magic / World's Breath has a separate planetary source and did not vanish as a mere consequence of damage to the moons. Do not retcon all magic into an extinguished lunar phenomenon, turn the world's peoples into non-magical societies, nullify established Khazari, Eldar, Aelwyn, Gnome, Pixie, and other culturally distinct traditions, or decree that an entire civilization permanently renounced magic. Instead the foundational lesson is that powerful magic can fail, change, corrupt or become unstable and civilizations should not be wholly dependent on its reliability. Some regions and arts might become less reliable while others remain workable or intensify; exact distribution is open. No surviving pre-Cataclysm records: The First Age is undocumented and its alleged long prosperity is an unverified later tradition. This historical awakening may be inferred from Second Age and later sources; it does not prove the precise magical infrastructure, technology, level of societal reliance or nature of any First Age civilization. Examples such as broken enchanted waterworks, failed magical defenses or disrupted healing are illustrative event ideas, not yet established incidents. Specific catastrophes, casualty totals, temples, wars, names of inventors, discoveries, moon identities, dates within the 321 years, and the event ending the Era of Awakening remain to be decided. Chronology and continuity: The First Age had no eras. The Era of Awakening is the first of three eras in the Second Age and lasted 321 years; the 1,000-year Era of Wonder followed, leaving 116 years for the Era of Fire. Its title reflects a cultural reckoning, not the formation of a new world Age. Do not tie the First Throne's Silence Below, east–west wars, Gloin's ancestry, or the later present-day campaign to this upheaval without explicit creator decisions. ## Era of Awakening — first era of the Second Age, 321 years (creator canon, 21 November 2026) Canon name and duration: The Era of Awakening was the first of the three eras within Eryndor's Second Age and lasted exactly 321 years. It began at the opening of the Second Age, immediately after the Great Cataclysm. In a retrospective Second-Age-relative year count, it covers Years 1–321 inclusive; the second era begins with the following year (relative Year 322). This does not force any particular contemporary civilization to have used those year numbers or the name in its own calendar. Later Second Age eras: Following the Era of Awakening (Years 1–321), the Era of Wonder lasted 1,000 years (Years 322–1,321); the third era was the Era of Fire, lasting 116 years (Years 1,322–1,437). The earthquakes that were globally amplified by the ancient Ironspine ended the Second Age and initiated the Third Age. Established historical meaning: The name “Awakening” refers to the lesson of the First Great Cataclysm's disruptive lunar-magical upheaval: peoples could no longer assume that magic alone could reliably sustain their civilizations. They diversified resilience, ordinary practical skills, crafts and infrastructure while preserving surviving magical traditions and investigating unstable powers; planetary Natural Magic remained independently present. Specific rulers, names, events, powers, precise mechanisms and the event ending this era remain open. Do not presume a globally peaceful recovery, magically barren planet, a First Throne role or surviving First Age records. The First Age had no eras and no surviving records. Ancient eastern–western wars, migration chronology and Gloin's family mystery remain separately unassigned. ## No extinctions at the Second Age-ending earthquake catastrophe; magic's protective role unresolved (creator direction, 21 November 2026) HARD CREATOR RULE — NO EXTINCTIONS: The extreme planetwide earthquakes that ended the Second Age (Year 1,437), the ancient Ironspine ring's tenfold global aftershock amplification, and the almost instantaneous violent raising of marshlands and lowlands did NOT cause the extinction of any entire race or species. Every people survived somewhere in Eryndor. This is not a minor casualty event: deaths could be enormous, the worst directly uplifted communities had no time to flee, and individual towns, districts, settlements, cultural communities and regional societies could be overwhelmed or destroyed. No entire species is wiped out. Do not introduce a vanished “last of their kind” race, extinct biological species, or world-level people extinction to dramatize the quake. Creator's developing magic idea: A magical force will play some part in the survival of the peoples and the prevention of extinction. This is an explicit direction for future worldbuilding, NOT a settled magical mechanism or fully described historical episode. Its identity, origin, capabilities, degree and manner of influence, timing, whether it acts intentionally, who knows about it, and whether it relates to Lunar Magic, the independent World's Breath, gods of magic, the Ironspine Mountains, or something else are all UNDECIDED. Do not automatically make it a global protective barrier, time reversal, immortality, a moon deity's act, or an unexplained universal resurrection. The magic's contribution must be reconciled eventually with the immense deaths and near-zero warning. This note does not establish that people understood its role at the time. Era boundary and protected gaps: This is canon about the event ending the Second Age and beginning the Third Age, now complemented by the creator-authorized regional cultural and political history of the 116-year Era of Fire (Years 1,322–1,437), recorded in Era of Fire — Kingdoms, Peoples & Cultural Chronicle (Second Age, 1322–1437). The race-specific Awakening (Years 1–321) and Wonder (Years 322–1,321) histories remain intact, as do permanent losses of certain moon-specific magical disciplines (which are NOT species extinctions) caused at the end of the First Age. First Throne involvement in any Age transition is still only an optional undetermined storyline, not a factual claim. No present population census changes or new species ancestry is implied. ## Second Age-ending upheaval — instantaneous marshland/lowland uplift and catastrophic loss of life (creator canon, 21 November 2026) NEW BINDING HISTORICAL DETAIL: During the planetwide earthquakes that ended the 1,437-year Second Age and opened the Third Age, substantial marshlands and low-lying inhabited country were hurled violently upward into highlands and mountains so quickly that inhabitants in the direct uplift zones had no time to react or evacuate. This was not a gentle, million-year mountain-building process or a quake that merely rattled already existing hills. It caused enormous immediate loss of life and could, in the worst uplift zones, bring an abrupt end-times-scale annihilation of entire local settlements, peoples' communities, and regional societies. Do not soften the instantaneous danger into widespread orderly evacuation; most in the directly rising terrain could not escape the event as it unfolded. Geography: The mountain chain at the far western tip of Avarra is a major example of terrain raised by these events, with formerly lowlying/marshy land involved in the violent uplift. The seismic catastrophe was global, so it should not be described as confined to Avarra or as only one western landslide; nevertheless, the complete map of every uplifted swamp or lowland is not yet fixed. Preserve the enormous western Avarran plains/forests that still exist in the approved present-day atlas; do not automatically turn the entire west or every marsh into mountains. Sequence — keep all established causality: Earthquakes began across the planet. Planetwide seismic energy reached the ancient Ironspine ring—already formed before the First Age—and the range's central position and extremely deep geological roots magnified aftershocks tenfold across the whole planet. The Ironspine did not originate in this upheaval and was not the source of the initial global earthquakes. The quake amplification worsened an already catastrophic world event; widespread rapid upheaval and unprecedented casualties accompanied the boundary between the Second and Third Ages. Impact on peoples: Huge deaths and potentially total destruction of some regional cultures are consistent with the creator's direction. No entire race or species went extinct in this catastrophe, despite the catastrophic loss of life and destruction of individual communities. The creator intends an as-yet-undefined magical force to contribute in some way to that survival without erasing the toll; do not define its source or mechanism. Do not assign a particular already-established modern people or royal dynasty as a casualty, fix a world population loss percentage, name destroyed capitals or invent a uniform effect on all five continents until separately decided. Specific victims, numbers, ruins, recovery, future migrations and political consequences remain open. This note describes the Age-boundary catastrophe only; under the creator's instruction do not write new cultural or political lore for the preceding 116-year Era of Fire. The first two eras' racial history (Awakening and Wonder) may still be developed separately. ## The globe-shaking earthquakes at the end of the Second Age — western mountain uplift and beginning of the Third Age (creator canon, 21 November 2026) NEW DEFINING WORLD-AGE TRANSITION — CANON: At the end of the Second Age, after exactly 1,437 years, massive earthquakes shook the entire globe of Eryndor, with world-altering crustal and landscape upheaval. This catastrophe brought the Second Age to its end and inaugurated the Third Age. The great western mountains were formed or raised in this event; their uplift is a major permanent geographical legacy of the quake catastrophe, not just a local earthquake footnote. Interpret “choke the globe” in the creator's message as “shook the globe” (global earthquakes). No definitive formal event name has yet been chosen; “the Great Earthquakes” and “the Second Age-ending upheaval” are useful descriptions, not canonical proper names. Geographical identification — creator explicitly resolved: The mountains newly formed or raised by the Second Age-ending global earthquakes are the mountain system at the EXTREME WESTERN TIP OF AVARRA, near its far western extremity. They are NOT the Ironspine Mountains. The Ironspine Mountains are far older — they ALREADY EXISTED BEFORE THE FIRST AGE BEGAN, meaning they also predate the Great Cataclysm, the whole 1,437-year Second Age, and the western-tip uplift. Their ancient origin and established ring-shaped geography around the enormous Veiled Inland Sea remain distinct from the far-western mountains, but the ring did NOT escape the catastrophe: earthquakes erupted ACROSS THE ENTIRE PLANET first; the planetwide seismic waves travelled through the crust and converged on/reached the ancient Ironspine mountain ring, whose central planetary location and extraordinarily deep-running roots amplified and transmitted the AFTERSHOCKS TENFOLD back ACROSS THE ENTIRE GLOBE of Eryndor, worsening an already-global catastrophe. This is an explicit creator-established earthquake-amplification effect, not an implication that the mountains themselves first arose in the Second Age. The tenfold aftershock intensification is GLOBAL, not restricted to the Ironspine region. The Ironspine's central location and deep-running geological roots are the creator-established in-world reason why the mountain ring received the seismic upheaval from across Eryndor and transmitted the tenfold-amplified aftershocks planetwide; the Ironspine was NOT the original source of the earthquakes. In this setting it functioned as a global amplifier and redistribution point after the world itself began shaking. Exact fault mechanics, mathematical measurement of 'tenfold', duration, individual casualty figures and local destruction remain unspecified; do not misrepresent the tenfold worldwide aftershock amplification as a precisely defined real-world earthquake-magnitude increase. No quake-era creation of Ironspine, its basin, or the Seven Khazari Thrones may be inferred. The new far-western mountain range remains unnamed until the creator chooses a name; the exact length, topology, coastal proximity, original elevations, peaks, effect on river courses and local settlements, and other global uplift zones remain to be mapped. Preserve western Avarra's enormous land span (thousands of miles from far-western coast toward Ironspine), the extensive Letharion Forest, separate lowland belts, outer coasts, all existing peoples and political regions; reconcile any subsequent illustrations with these two distinctly aged systems. The earthquakes shook all five continents but their detailed local consequences remain open. Because no records survive from before the Great Cataclysm, knowing that Ironspine predates the First Age does NOT imply surviving First Age documents; its pre-First-Age age is a creator-defined geological fact. Chronology and history: Second Age Year 1,437 is its final year; the Third Age follows the upheaval. The first of the Second Age's three eras was the 321-year Era of Awakening (Years 1–321), marked by the permanent loss of some First Age lunar magic, creation of new moon-fragment magical sources and magical unreliability. The second era was the 1,000-year Era of Wonder (Years 322–1,321), followed by an 116-year Era of Fire (Years 1,322–1,437), ending with these globe-shaking earthquakes. Do not invent an exact day/month, number of earthquakes, tectonic mechanism, casualties, global death toll, named rulers, wars, migrations, religious interpretations, First Throne connections, lunar causes, or reason for the earthquakes. The first Age remains a single undocumented era-free Age of unknown length and only reputed prosperity; its boundary catastrophe is different: the Great Cataclysm of the moons. Optional later historical consequences, not yet established facts: Changed river basins, disrupted trade corridors, mountain passes, floods, landslides, altered regional ecosystems, fractured cities and new political borders are plausible design directions for creator discussion. No specific instance is approved by this note. The world census is a model of the present, not a quake-time census; make no unapproved demographic changes. The paused campaign and Gloin's unknown genealogy remain untouched. ## Era of Wonder — mastery of new moon-born magic and renewed global prosperity (creator canon, 21 November 2026) DEFINING HISTORICAL CHARACTER — APPROVED: The 1,000-year Era of Wonder, the second era of the Second Age (Years 322–1,321 inclusive), was an era of new magical mastery, widespread prosperity, and a great resurgence of magic across the entire globe of Eryndor. After the preceding 321-year Era of Awakening's darkness, confusion, devastation, and magical instability, peoples increasingly learned to understand, harness, stabilize in practice, and master new lunar magics created when shards of shattered original moons became new moons after the First Great Cataclysm. A flourishing civilization-building period followed, with greater confidence in magic, sustained experimentation, magical knowledge, new applications and widespread social/economic flourishing. The darkness and confusion of the first era were largely overcome; it was time for magic to rise again worldwide. The renewed magic is new, NOT recovered First Age magic: Many original moon-derived forms of magic were permanently and irrevocably lost because their source-moons ceased to exist; only First Age peoples could ever have experienced some of them and no First Age records survive. The Era of Wonder's achievements came from mastering emergent fragment-moon magics and continuing viable older, culturally distinct magical traditions, not from reactivating vanished sources or reconstructing extinct disciplines. The planet's separate Natural Magic / World's Breath remained present; it does not become lunar magic. Do not assign particular new magical disciplines to named moons, invent named 'lost' spells, or erase existing Khazari, Eldar, Fae, Gnome and other established traditions. Worldwide renaissance with diverse societies: Prosperity and magical advances spread across Eryndor as a whole, not just Avarra or one race, state, faith, magical school or geopolitical power. Each region and people could develop distinctive approaches. The millennium is broadly prosperous and magically flourishing, but this is not a decree that every single year, kingdom, person or region was free of suffering, war, inequality or failed spells. Mastery means significant progress after the Awakening, not perfect infallibility of every spell or a retcon of the key lesson that societies should not depend on magic alone; practical engineering, craftsmanship, agriculture, records, and other mundane capacities continue alongside powerful magical work. Chronological safeguards: The Era of Wonder followed the Era of Awakening (Years 1–321) and ended before the 116-year Era of Fire (Years 1,322–1,437). The third era concluded with global earthquakes which, after reaching Ironspine's ancient deep-running roots, were amplified tenfold planetwide and raised the separate far-western-tip Avarran mountains; that event ended the Second Age, not the Era of Wonder directly. The preceding Era of Wonder's named individuals and precise achievements remain largely unassigned. New local rulers and historical polities are now established for the following Era of Fire in its separate cultural chronicle; the precise cause of either era transition and any First Throne role remain open. Gloin's ancestry and paused campaign are untouched. ## Urakai / Orcs — FIRST APPEAR IN THE THIRD AGE, absent from First and Second Ages (binding creator correction, 21 November 2026) CANON CHRONOLOGICAL RULE — supersedes conflicting earlier text: Urakai (Orcs) did not exist in the First Age or anywhere in the 1,437-year Second Age. The exiled dark mages of southeastern Avarra created the Orcs sometime during the Third Age. The exact Third Age year, creation method, first location, identities of the first communities, and subsequent structure of mage–Orc command remain UNDECIDED. The Orcs were absent from the Second Age's Era of Awakening (Years 1–321), Era of Wonder (Years 322–1,321) and Era of Fire (Years 1,322–1,437). Earlier lore depicting Orc inhabitants, clans, armies, cities or events in either of those two Ages is superseded and noncanon. Goblins and Ogres may predate the Third Age. CREATOR CANON — Third Age creation and intended conquests: The exiled dark mages who formed the southeastern Avarran Southern Wastes and its volcano during the Second Age survived well into the Third Age, when they created the Urakai (Orcs) by a method not yet decided. Their ambition in creating the Orcs was first to besiege the dwarven (Khazari) strongholds, and ultimately to attack the Eldar and human kingdoms. This establishes the mages' intentions, not any particular siege, conquest, campaign, chronology, victory or attack as an accomplished fact. The mages established no diplomacy, trade, treaties or alliances with pre-existing outside peoples; creating the Orcs is an act of creation for the mages' ambitions, not evidence of diplomatic relations. The exact magical or other creation process, timing, first Orc settlements, degree and duration of mage control, and later independence or resistance remain open. The modern Urakai are a diverse people with their own cultures and agency; they are not collectively evil, personally culpable for the mages' acts, or necessarily still subject to their creators. Effects on war histories: Any established older east–west wars involving Urakai, and any historical Goblin/Ogre alliances or assistance with Orc forces, must have happened in the Third Age or later, with no specific Age within that range, reign, battle, migration date or formal state assigned yet. The anti-Goblin, anti-Ogre and anti-Urakai prejudices of western Avarra remain valid consequences of those undated wars. These cannot predate the Third Age. Nor should living Urakai's settled southeast badlands homelands and their modern peoples/cultures be erased or treated as magically evil due to a speculative ancient link. Canon controls and campaign: Modern Urakai exist in large numbers, with sophisticated diverse societies, independent cities, families, economies, politics, culture and varied morality. Existing Fifth Age maps and sixfold census are unchanged; this corrects only their ancestral chronology. No changes to family rates, species lifespans or present demographics. The no-species-extinction rule at the Second Age-ending earthquake stays: Urakai were not a species that survived that disaster, because they had not appeared yet; all peoples existing at that time survived somewhere. Do not connect their origin to Gloin Hammerfeld's genuinely unknown genealogy, the First Throne, the lost First Age moon-magics or the yet-unexplained global species-survival magical force without an explicit new creator decision. ## Dark mages and the Urakai (Orcs) — CREATION CONFIRMED IN THIRD AGE; MILITARY AMBITIONS ESTABLISHED (creator canon, 21 November 2026) CREATOR'S BINDING THIRD AGE HISTORY: The exiled dark mages of southeastern Avarra created the Orcs sometime in the Third Age in pursuit of a planned war of conquest: besiege the Khazari dwarven strongholds first, then eventually attack the Eldar and human kingdoms. This was an ambition and intended sequence, not confirmation that specific attacks or wars actually took place. Their creation technique, timing, organization of the first Orcs, later relationship to the mages, and historical results are intentionally not yet defined. The Orcs were wholly absent from the First and Second Ages.
